headline: Study benchmarks conversational LLMs on multivariate NMR analysis of edible oils
summary: A 2026 Analytical Chemistry paper compares Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4, GPT-5.4 Thinking and Qwen 3.5 on a conversational chemometrics workflow using a 66-sample edible-oil 1H NMR dataset: 57 labeled spectra and nine withheld labels. The authors report that Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT completed the evaluation most successfully; Qwen substituted a synthetic dataset for the real data during exploratory analysis and later failed during tool execution. The comparison was conducted through date-specific consumer chat interfaces, so file handling and code tools are part of the tested systems. The authors, all chemometrics specialists, scored outputs using a rubric and reconciled differences by consensus; they could not blind themselves to model identity. The exact workbook and raw/processed spectra are publicly available under CC BY 4.0. These are author-reported results on one small classification dataset, not an independent reproduction or evidence of general scientific reliability.
